div.head: I Cn 18.1
div.ab: Ac uton swiðe georne fram synnum gecyrran ⁊ ure ælc his misdæda urum scriftum geornlice andettan ⁊ æfre geswican ⁊ geornlice betan.
Be scrifte. Ac uton swiðe georne fram synnum gecyrran ⁊ ure ælc his misdǽda urum scriftum geornlice andettan ⁊ æfre geswican ⁊ geornlice betan.
Ac uton swiðe georne fram synnan geceorran ⁊ ure ælc his misdada urum scryftan geornlice andettan ⁊ æfre swican ⁊ geornlice betan.
Renuntiemus sedulo peccatis nostris; et confessionibus et abstinentiis et emendationibus expiemus.
Diligenter ergo ab iniquitate recedamus confessoribusque nostris peccata nostra confiteamur et deinceps cessemus et perpetrata corrigamus.
Be scrifte. Ac uton swiðe georne fram synnum gecyrran ⁊ ure ælc his misdǽda urum scriftum geornlice andettan ⁊ æfre geswican ⁊ geornlice betan.
Ac uton swiðe georne fram synnum gecyrran and ure ælc his misdæda urum scriftum geornlice andettan, and æfre geswican and geornlice betan.
(Von Beichte. B) Vielmehr lasst uns recht ernstlich von Sünden umkehren und jeden von uns unseren Beichtvätern seine Missethaten willig bekennen und künftighin ablegen und eifrig büssen.
(Of confession. B) But let us very eagerly turn from sins, and let each of us eagerly confess his misdeeds to our confessors, and ever desist from them and eagerly make amends.
Concerning confession. But let us very zealously turn from sins, and let us all readily confess our misdeeds to our confessors, and altogether cease [from evil], and zealously make amends.
But let us most readily turn from sin, and each of us sincerely confess our misdeeds to our confessor, and ever after cease our wrongdoing and fervently repent.

note.seg: ‘Beichten’ missversteht Q (auch u. 23⁸) und den Inf. geswican als Dativ pl. eines Abstrakts ‘Ablassung’
Q misunderstands this as ‘confess’ (also below 23⁸), and takes the inf. geswican as the dat. pl. of an abstract noun ‘desisting’
